basis: Defined by disease of ocular adnexa, including eyelids, conjunctiva and lacrimal apparatus.
Mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia are defining manifestations.
Inherited erythrocytosis; elevated erythropoietin does not itself establish endocrine-organ disease.
Achalasia and generalized lipodystrophy; corneal opacity and sensorineural hearing loss each 5/5. Neurologic, skin and skeletal findings omitted by cap; valve disease 1/4.
Congenital cervical skin and subcutaneous defect; neck restriction results from local scarring. Other malformations are occasional associations.
Epithelial carcinoma located in lymph nodes; nodal tissue has no dedicated axis. This is not lymphoma or a blood-cell neoplasm.
Neoplasm occupying bone marrow, whether primary or metastatic; marrow belongs to the haematologic axis.
Malignant bone-forming tumor arising in bone; pulmonary metastasis is not a defining or sufficiently common manifestation across the group.
Germ cell malignancy arising in the ovary, a reproductive site; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
AQP4-associated autoimmune disease defined by CNS inflammation and optic neuropathy; optic nerve involvement belongs to ocular.
OEIS defines bladder, bowel and spinal defects; myelomeningocele is frequent. Skeletal malformations, including hip dislocation and vertebral defects, occur in 30-79%.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 80-99%; structural abnormalities of other organs are predominantly below 30%.
Benign fibrohistiocytic tumor arising in subcutaneous tissue or deep connective soft tissue.
Developmental disorder of intestinal enteric nerve plexuses causing colonic dysfunction; both bowel and peripheral autonomic neurons define the disease.
Somatostatin-producing endocrine-cell neoplasm arising in the jejunum.
Benign perineurial nerve-sheath tumor typically arising in dermis or subcutis of the hands; extraneural denotes growth outside a named nerve.
Mitochondrial disorder with progressive CNS disease; visual impairment 2/3, optic atrophy 1/3 and WPW conduction abnormality 2/3 support eye and cardiac involvement.
Immune dysregulation with autoimmune cytopenias and lymphoproliferation; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage. Lymphoma is a later risk.
Benign dermal melanocytosis; melanoma is very rare and separately diagnosed.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive CNS dysfunction; skeletal dysplasia includes scoliosis and platyspondyly (1/1 reported). Ocular damage frequency is uncertain.
Seronegative immune-mediated inflammatory disease defined by CNS and optic nerve attacks; absent antibodies do not exclude its immune mechanism.
Childhood germ cell tumor originating in the ovary; reproductive tumor origin has no axis.
Bone fragility and skeletal deformities define BMP1-related osteogenesis imperfecta. Blue sclerae and hirsutism do not establish functional organ damage.
Defective airway ciliary clearance with bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 15/16. Structural heart defects are uncommon; situs inversus alone is not damage.
Progressive skeletal muscle dystrophy; cardiomyopathy is annotated at 5-29%, below threshold. Speech delay alone does not establish direct CNS involvement.
